observations: Photo 0: one white plastic electric iron standing on its heel on a tiled floor.
Photo 0: a temperature dial sits under the handle; no steam tank, spray nozzle or water window is visible, consistent with a dry iron.
Photo 0: the soleplate edge shows a dark metal rim; the soleplate face itself is not shown.
Photo 0: the cloth-covered cord is dirty and frayed where it leaves the iron, and has a visible joint near the left with tape and loose coloured wire, which looks like a home splice or repair.
Photo 0: the cord ends in a UK style three pin plug.
Photo 0: the body is scuffed and stained; no brand name, model or rating plate is readable.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a used iron with a dial and no visible steam features.
No clip of it plugged in and heating; the spliced, frayed cord in photo 0 raises doubt.

risks.risk: Iron may not heat or the thermostat may be faulty.
risks.proof: A clip of the iron plugged in, the dial turned up, the indicator light on, and water drops sizzling on the soleplate.

risks.risk: Cord is frayed and spliced, a shock and fire risk that likely needs a new cord.
risks.proof: A close photo of the cord along its full length and the joint, showing whether bare wire is exposed.

risks.risk: Soleplate may be scratched, burnt or rusted, which marks clothes.
risks.proof: A photo of the soleplate face in good light.

proof_requests: A clip of the iron plugged in and heating, with the indicator light on and water sizzling on the soleplate.
A close photo of the cord splice and the full cord length.
A photo of the soleplate face.
A photo of the rating plate or label under the heel or handle.
response.reason: The item is plainly a used dry iron and can be priced by type at its worst case, as not working with a cord that needs replacing, until a heating clip and cord close-up are sent.
